idiom_name: newtype struct implementing the expected trait by delegating to the inner value
implementation_notes: Rust has no delegation, so the adapter is a newtype - a single-field tuple struct or a named-field struct - that implements the trait the caller expects and forwards each method to the value it holds. This is not politeness but coherence: when the trait and the type are both foreign, the orphan rule forbids `impl ForeignTrait for ForeignType`, and the local newtype is the only way to add the implementation. Store ownership or a borrow explicitly (struct Adapter(Inner) versus struct Adapter<'a>(&'a Inner)) and expose into_inner/as_inner when callers must recover the value; do not implement Deref to shortcut the forwarding, because the API guidelines reserve Deref for smart pointers and it punches a hole through the adapter's boundary.
pitfalls: The orphan rule forces the newtype, and the newtype changes the type in every signature that used to take the inner value.

A newtype loses the inner type's trait implementations (Display, Clone, PartialOrd...), which forces forwarding boilerplate: derive what you can and re-implement deliberately rather than reaching for Deref.
`struct Adapter<'a>(&'a Inner)` ties the adapter to the borrow - it cannot outlive the inner value, which is what prevents dangling adapters but also forbids storing it beyond the borrow.
Coherence blocks shortcuts: you cannot blanket-implement a foreign trait for foreign types, and a local blanket impl over a foreign bound risks conflicting with future upstream impls.

variants.name: Extension trait implemented on the existing type
variants.implementation_notes: Instead of wrapping the foreign type, define your own (extension) trait in your crate and implement it for the foreign type - legal under the orphan rule because the trait is local - returning the adapter value from a method on it. No newtype appears in signatures, call sites read as ordinary methods, and lifetimes stay untouched; the trade is that the adapter is no longer a distinct type, so it cannot be stored as a named value or given state without a wrapper after all.
variants.idiom_name: trait AdapterExt { fn applicator(&self) -> impl Applicator; }
pitfalls: Extension traits are only usable where the trait is imported, so an unreachable impl is invisible to callers.
Returning `impl Trait` hides the adapter's concrete type: fine for callers, but the type cannot be named in APIs that need it.
The extension adds methods to a foreign type, so a future upstream method of the same name can collide; resolution then silently prefers the inherent method.
